The call was placed on my cell-phone and a number of XXXX appeared. When I called, no one answered. I was again contacted on XX/XX/XXXX with the caller id showing XXXX, KS again I answered and no response. This time it showed a number of XXXX, which I called back and spoke with XXXX XXXX who identified himself as a collector for Stellar Recovery in an attempt to make a demand on a debt to XXXX XXXX from XX/XX/XXXX. When I advised XXXX XXXX this account was past the statute of limitations he said No it certainly is not. Before I progress with the rest of the facts, let me state under Kansas States Annotated 60-511 A creditor must bring an action-based on a contract that is expressed or implied but not in writing, an oral contract within three years. As there was never any written contract for service this was in-fact a time bared account. This act of collecting on a time barred account in its own is in violation of 15 USC 1692e subsections 807 ( 2 ) ( A ), as the legal status of the account is time barred to which XXXX XXXX disagreed with, keep in mind, his answer must be truthful under the FDCPA. I was then transferred to a supervisor XXXX XXXX and asked why my caller ID just shows XXXX, KS to which she stated We use an auto-dialer ). This is in violation of two laws. First, the TCPA that The FCC has determined that debt collection calls are not telemarketing calls. Therefore, under the rule the FCC has stated that with respect to autodialed or prerecorded debt collection calls, to the extent that they do not contain telemarketing messages, would not require any consent when made to residential wire line consumers, but require either prior written or oral consent if made to a consumers wireless number referring to 47 C.F.R. 64.1200 ( a ) ( 1 ). At no point, did I ever consent to my personal cell-phone number to be called. Additionally, the way your caller ID shows is XXXX, KS, but it is not just the name that I argue is a violation of law, it is the fact that the phone number that appears is a XXXX, KS number, when your office is clearly in Florida. Such action constitutes a violation of the 15 U.S. Code Section 1692f ( 5 ) Causing charges to be made to any person for communication by concealment of the true purpose of the communication. Obviously I have the right to determine what calls to accept and what ones not to answer. By concealing the true caller on the caller ID, your office has engaged in deceptive practices and as XXXX XXXX admits this is an auto-dialer, I am wiling to bet I am not the only consumer for whom your office has done this to. CONVERGENT OUTSOURCING , INC . 
XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX There is a regulation under the FDIC Act known as Regulation 5000, which acknowledges an unsecured debt as a different classification from standard to sub-standard. On day 120 of default, all interest, late fees and overdraft fees cease, and the basis of debt id re-evaluated. On each of these collections the standard has been violated as both entities are using a 180-day default method, which means both the accounting and its subsequent collection process is a violation of my rights under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act. In essence, both collection processes are VOID, and must be recalled by their respective original creditor. I am a XXXX American citizen who believes that my rights are being violated and my civil rights are in total violation under the Civil Rights Act. 
I make the following demands : XXXX ) A true copy original of my credit application, and XXXX ) A complete accounting under FDIC Regulation XXXX guidelines. 
I, XXXX XXXX believes in the credit reporting system as the most important element to the success of the commercial banking system. I am also a proponent of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) as a tool to streamline issues on credit reports that may be dragging down my overall scores. Accordingly, I address each particular issue directly with the creditor in question, before submitting any complaint to the credit bureaus if necessary. Therefore, I desire the following reinvestigation as follows : 1 ) On accounts where late payments are posted, I respectfully request a review of the past payment history and to ascertain if certain payments could actually have been posted late because of an overlap on the 30-days grace period. I realize that this may happen on occasion, and I request only a summary review internally, and do not require any documentation. 
2 ) On any account that falls within the 84-month negative reporting timeline, I respectfully request either the deletion of the account if said account was closed, or the elimination of the prior payment if the account it is still active, this is well within the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) guidelines pertaining to obsolete information. 
3 ) Any collections must be proved if either a direct collection and/or debt purchase. In either event I request that a true original copy of right to pursue collection be established with each respective credit reporting agency, and if a debt purchase the guidelines proving transfer of ownership must be submitted to all credit bureaus as well as me personally to validate ownership and the right to collect. I am well within my rights requesting proper documentation as administered through the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) and the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ), in addition to the even stricter guidelines enforced by the office of attorney general in my state of domicile. 
I respectfully request each investigation to be reported to XXXX, XXXX and XXXX XXXX within a reasonable time period, hopefully 30-days. I realize that the current Covid-19 crisis could cause delays, so the best efforts of each financial institution and collection agency will be appreciated under the current circumstances. 
XXXX XXXX

I am applying for a loan since beginning of XX/XX/2020, to buy a property. My credit score was good, but since I had a medical debt, my lending company thought it was best to pay off the debt so that my credit score could go up of many points more and it would be great for my application. The only thing that I had to do for it was to call ALLIED DEBT COLLECTOR and pay it off and get a proof that the debt was paid off. So I called the first time on XX/XX/XXXX to resolve my case and paid my amount due of {$250.00} for XXXX in one single payment. I was told by XXXX that it would take 60-90 days for the credit bureau to show it online. Explaining that I needed a proof ASAP for my lending company that my debt was paid off, I asked if I could get a proof send by email. I was told no, they never send anything by email but by mail. I gave my full address and was told that the letter would be sent right after the debt was collected, which as the next day. 
I have since, checked my mailbox every single day. I NEVER got any mail that is more important than just store advertisement. I called my banker several times on recorded line talking and keeping updates on weather this letter came into my mail or not, and the answer was always NO of course. 
In the last 10 days I tried to contact ALLIED again several times, at least 5 times without any response. Then I contacted my banker again explaining that it has been over 35 days since the debt was paid, that nobody was answering the phone at ALLIED and that on my XXXX XXXX it was showing that the debt is paid but I could not do anything without this letter. Few days ago my banker told me that my credit score went down! I was shocked since I have nothing else, no debt at that point, credit cards all paid off and no late payments. my banker said that the only way for me to have that number up again, being able to close the loan AND the closing of the property is to get this proof from ALLIED. That is the only thing that put everything on hold. There is NO other way. The closing date has also been postponed several times. 

So I called ALLIED again and spoke to a first person ( don't remember the name ), then to an XXXX, then to another person, then to XXXX and then again to XXXX. To all of them I explained my request of the importance of this letter and proof of pay off and that the letter never came in my mail. I asked to all of them if it was possible to resent this letter to me in a faster way, such as email or fax or expedited. 

The only thing that made sense of all the conversations and calls is that they all said was : " the account was closed on XX/XX/XXXX ''. " it takes 60-90 days to remove it from the bureau ''. 
Otherwise, one person told me : " the letter was sent out the next day '', " it has to be reviewed before sending, then it gets in your mail after 20 business days '', or " we never send a second letter, or same letter twice. Once it is send out, it is over '' Another said : " we never sent out letters once it is paid off '' Another one said : " we sent out letters 14days after the payment has been made, then it takes another 7 to 14 business days to get to your mail '' or also " well for us, the letter has been sent out so whatever else is none of our business and there is nothing else we can do ''. 
One person said : " we can send it to you by email, but not the same letter that the bureau but a proof of account paid off. '' Last night I had checked my credit score and credit informations online, where it was written that the debt was closed online on XX/XX/XXXX. So none of the phone conversations made sense with what was showing online. 

Regarding the call operators, one of them did not appreciate that I requested to talk to a supervisor, he said that the supervisor would " maybe '' call me back but that was not sure. I could not even speak to the accountant department, because I was not allowed to. Someone else told me that today the request to talk to a supervisor could be made and the supervisor would " maybe '' call me within 42-72hours,  but not even certain of it. Although I said it was an extremely urgent matter. There was nothing to do beside waiting the " uncertain '' phone call and also IF the supervisor would be able to send another letter or any proof of any way. 

I was also told over the phone that I had to check with my local post office, which I did but there was nothing for me. But also told : " For us it was sent out, so ... it is not up to us ''. I even proposed to pay for an overnight expedited mail, but was told that this is not up to us anymore since it had to be reviewed before mailing out. '' A review from the accountant department before mailing a copy of the letter that was already paid over a month ago and sent out? 

I am now in stand-by stupidly waiting to get an answer, phone or just a proof by mail ( if it was ever sent out, which I truly don't believe so ). If sent, why is it also so difficult to sent the same letter a second time? It is not my fault if I never got it. 

Nobody cared enough. I called my banker several times again, all phone calls are recorded by them so I have proof of that, and I know your phone calls are recorded too. 

I told everyone how extremely important and urgent this situation was for me, for my loan, to get a new copy because I never got the mail and I was supposed to do the closing for my property already Monday XXXX, then postponed 2 more times. Now probably another time but I don't even know when. The seller is getter me in trouble for it, the title company is seeking for explanations, my real estate agent has more work to do. I have no idea what to tell them. I am lost, confused, stressed out, frustrated and lied to. All of this for one single letter that would unblock everything for my husband and I. It makes me look very unprofessional in front of everyone. All this for a small loan that has been ready to be send to the title company weeks ago. Just for this matter my husband and I are ashamed. 

Allied has not been cooperative in any way. This situation is extremely ridiculous!

state: When i process a charge through my debit account, the transaction will appear on my online banking app as " processing ''. This amount that is processing is deducted from my overall available balance, and reflect in my available balance. The bank has confirmed this to be true. Once a transaction is issued into pending status, the funds from that transaction, are no longer available. However, days later, when my bank account avail balance falls below the " pending '' charges amount, the status of the charge changes from pending to processed, and my account falls negative. They then return the transaction and charge me a fee unless i deposit funds, or my savings account balance transfers and covers the transaction. This is alarming because, originally, the charge was already deducted from my balance, and appeared as not avail. and was allocated to the transaction. This has been an ongoing incident and i have mentioned this to the bank on numerous occasions. Transactions will sit in " pending '' status for days and days, being processed up to 7 days after the initial transaction. In many cases, the funds process once my account balance falls below the amount of the pending transactions, in which case i am charged a fee and the payment is returned. The most recent incident, was the bank reflecting 6 charges that had been processed days earlier as " completed '' and paid. They used my savings account to cover the charges, and i had no access to my savings account money, in order to transfer, or withdraw. The bank places my funds from the savings account on " hold '' to pay the transactions that could not be covered by my checking account. On my mobile banking app, and as well as at the bank, these 7 charges reflected as " completed '' and paid. However, later in the morning a transaction from XXXX came through my account and over drafted my account. This was a XXXX error and has happened in the past. I was educated by the bank the previous times i needed to call the merchant. In which case, i was going to allow the bank to return it, and contact XXXX directly. The next day, Santander returned all transactions on my account and charged me 8 over draft fees. I called and was told XXXX came out FIRST and was the reason the rest went over drafted ( payments that had already been in a pending status and reflected as taken out of my avail balance days before ) I requested a transcript from the bank, indicating this as the case, since my negative balance ONLY reflected the XXXX transaction, and not all 8. As a consumer, that would look as if, everything else went through and processed except the one XXXX charge. This is exactly what the bank account reflected. I then spoke to a supervisor who explained everything was processed at the end of the day, and if the funds aren't avail in checking or savings everything rejects. I elaborated that my bank account did NOT reflect that, and there was no way for me as a consumer to know, those items were not paid, she offered to return up to 3 fees, but that i was responsible for the rest because it was not their error. I elaborated again, that when something is indicated as pending, the funds for that charge are removed from your account, and placed on hold. This was again confirmed. In which case, when the 7 pay pal transactions were placed on hold, the funds were removed, allocated to pay the XXXX charges, and were not available for me to spend out of my account. Yet, when they were completed on XX/XX/XXXX, they caused me to become over drafted due to the funds being " unavailable ''. I was charged 8x for returned items, that they had said, were deducted when placed into a " pending '' status. This is a common occurrence. I have to continuously monitor my account and keep extra funds in order to avoid being charged a fee when the bank decides to move the status from pending to completed. Even after being reflected in my balance. The last tine this happened i was told the computer " glitches '' if too many items are processed and returned at once, in which case it returns all of them. No one could provide me a transcript of my charges or funds, and i was told this is how this bank " works '' double charging customers, or misleading customers into believing an item is paid, and completed, only to return it the next day, or 2 days later. There is no way to guarantee an item as paid, and available funds, since the bank misleads its customers with the online banking by showing items as paid, but then returning them. There is no way to ensure the consumer, the items are paid, when the online banking is not reflecting accurately.

state:
On XX/XX/XXXX, I received an email from Chase, where I have a credit card, that was asking if I recognized a charge of {$170.00} at XXXX XXXX  that was declined. I responded by selecting 'No ' in the email and checked my online banking app for other activity that was potentially fraudulent. There were four other transactions from that same day that I did not recognize and believed were fraudulent. ( My partner is an authorized user on the account with a card, and she did not recognize the transactions either ). I contacted Chase by phone and notified them that I had both cards in my possession and that I did not recognize the charges, believing them to be fraudulent. Within a day or two, the charges were subsequently removed from the list of recent transactions appearing in the mobile banking app. 
The four charges, totaling {$400.00}, included : {$100.00} - XXXX # XXXX {$110.00} - XXXX  # XXXX {$170.00} - XXXX XXXX {$11.00} - XXXX XXXX XXXX On XX/XX/XXXX, I missed a call from Chase, who then called my parents ( whose phone number may have been previously listed as an additional contact # ). I called Chase back and was told that the charges would be rebilled to my account. The only explanation given was that their system said the card chip was used for the charges, and that it is impossible to counterfeit the chip in their card. I repeated the fact that neither I, nor my authorized user, made those purchases, and that I did not agree with their decision to rebill them to my account. 
Given the limited explanation for rebilling I asked to speak with someone who was familiar with the decision, or who was involved in making the determination to rebill. I was told I would receive a call back after the holiday weekend, but that the transactions would post to my account that day. 
After not receiving any further communication from Chase, I schedule a call with a banker at my local branch on XX/XX/XXXX and explained the situation to her. She was very sympathetic, understanding, and professional, but after she transferred me to the fraud prevention team I received the same response. That because it is impossible for Chase 's chip to be compromised, I was responsible for the charges. I asked if there was any additional detail regarding the charges or merchants that could help me understand what had been purchased, or where exactly. The fraud recovery analyst ( XXXX ) told me that there was no additional information he was able to see regarding the transactions, but that I could escalate the case for a second review of the charges. I was surprised that a secondary review had not already been initiated given my initial disagreement with the rebilling, but responded that I wanted the case to be escalated. I also asked him how the XXXX XXXX charge of XXXX ( that had been declined ) was coded, and he said the chip was present. I am still looking for an explanation of how that charge ( that was attempted with the chip present ) could be considered fraudulent and declined, but that other charges made with the chip that I am disputing are standing because " it is impossible to clone or compromise the chip ''. 
I have still not heard from Chase 's fraud recovery team as of XX/XX/XXXX. 
The banker at my local branch in XXXX 's XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) submitted a customer complaint on my behalf given my frustrating experience dealing with these fraudulent charges being rebilled, and I have since received a call and voicemail from Chase 's branch complaints team regarding my experience. While I intend to call them back and discuss my poor customer experience with the fraud team, I feel it is important to bring to the CFPB 's attention the way Chase handles disputed/fraudulent charges. I have been been a cardholder with Chase for at least five years, and have never given them any reason to doubt my assertion that these charges are fraudulent. Because the transaction codes show the chip as present at the transaction, and they believe that the chip can not be compromised, they do not consider fraud as possibility and as such, have not performed a good-faith review of the charges following notification from a customer that they are suspected as fraud. Relying on that chip, and the validity of the transaction codes, should not release them from duty of care to their customers to actually review a charge reported as fraud. When I asked about one of the vendors ( XXXX XXXX XXXX I was told no information was available on them. 
Thank you for your review.

I was in Forbearance with my mortgage lender due to XXXX XXXX related financial hardships, they gave me a 2 month extension on my forbearance, giving it an end date of XX/XX/2022. I spoke with them shortly before the end of my forbearance period was to commence, and they informed me they would be sending a packet/application to be filled out for their Underwriting Dept to review the best options moving forward with the reconvening of my loan payments while address the additional Forbearance deficit. On XX/XX/XXXX, on the launch date of the government HAF program-XXXX XXXX I immediately applied. My application was submitted fully complete with all required supporting documentation. I was contacted the following week to re-sign two authorization forms, which I did within that week and re-submitted. All required documents and phases of my application have been completed-time and date stamp, XX/XX/2022 @ XXXX. During my last conversations at the end of XXXX XXXX with my lenderXXXX XXXX. I was advised my loan was potentially being sold. I was advised any payments granted by the XXXX would be submitted to the new lender when their information became available. I was told in the meantime I would still be receiving the packet my lender had previously told me would be sent out in XX/XX/2022, at the commencing of my ( extended ) Forbearance period. I was also advised I should not make any payments until they were able to review my completed paperwork-as it would not be applied to any current payments due. 
In XXXX and XXXX a man came to my home taking pictures-advising my loan has been reassigned and that he was simply conducting routine monthly photographs per the lender. He was unable to give me any documentation nor provide me the name or contact info for my new servicer. In XXXX I began receiving calls from a XXXX number, I typically do not answer such numbers, assuming them to likely be spam. At the end of XXXX one of the calls resulted in a voicemail left on my cell phone-upon listening to the message I was made aware that a company by the name of AmeriHome was trying to contact me. Still assuming it was likely a sales solicitation to refinance, I returned the call. After several transfers, I was told that I was in an active foreclosure with a sales day, a month away on XXXX XXXX. I was in complete shock and demanded to understand how this could be. I was given a state local number to call, and told that I needed to speak to someone at that number, as they were the foreclosure dept. When I tried to explain that I was in the middle of completing my next steps to proceed at the close of my forbearance when my loan was apparently transferred to them without proper notice or instruction as how to contact or proceed with the new servicer-I was met with ghastly denial and was in fact told that they ( AmeriHome ) has always had my loan. 
I was told that they would send a packet out that must be completed before the XXXX to avoid sale but would take 7-10 business days to arrive. Once again advised to call the foreclosure department. I hung up and proceeded to call the number provided, and I reached a legal office. I left a voicemail on a Friday afternoon at XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX. I was in a complete panic, overcome with worry, confusion, and immense anxiety the entire weekend. I looked up my application status on XXXX and found the status stating XXXX XXXX Authorization Needed-set up. This lead me to believe they have been waiting on a response from the mortgage company to proceed with funding disbursement. On Monday I contacted the XXXX customer service line promptly at XXXX. The associate I spoke with advised she would unlock my account and I was to update the section of the application regarding my mortgage lenders contact info. She proceeded to hang up on me when I inquired further as to how to ensure this would be addressed and that I had a time sensitive foreclosure sale impeding. I went through my unopened mail and found a statement from XXXX most recent from AmeriHome and XXXX other correspondence from XX/XX/2022, also a payment statement. No where did it indicate I was in default or in threat of foreclosure. It did mention my delinquent payments-from my forbearance period, though the forbearance itself was not mentioned at all. There was a piece of paper with a Hud Counseling agencys contact info include separately, stating it was provide by the law office whom I had contacted on the previous Friday and indicated it was on behalf of them and XXXX XXXX dba XXXX XXXX?? Yet another mortgage name given, making it impossible to decipher what information I should even update my XXXX app with to ensure it the correct lender and mortgagee clause be provided. I was able to schedule a phone appt for later that day with XXXX of the HUD counselors from the agency provided in that included sheet of paper. She proved to be a wonderful and most helpful resource. She struggled to find any indication of AmeriHome as having a judgment or even a delinquent account status reported to my credit, she could not find any info on the upcoming sheriff sale that had been mentioned by two diff dates in the one phone conversation I had with AmeriHome. She advised I reach out to my local sheriffs office, which I did and they were unable to find any information on a foreclosure sale of my home, let along a scheduled auction sale in a month. I decided to try the law firm again, as they had not returned my call/message from Friday and the HUD counselor thought they might have more info as to the true status of my mortgage and verify or deny upcoming sale. I was advised they would have had to attempted to contact me 5 weeks prior to the scheduled sales date and on 3 occasions. I was transferred several times within the lawyers office staff voicemails, 2 of which were full and I could not even leave a message. I called back and demand I be able to speak with someone, I would hold if need be but I had a time pertinent matter to address. Finally I was given a staff member who proceeded to tell me she didnt know what I was seeking, that my loan servicer was Cenlar-after I had to stop her and request she spell it, as this was yet another lender I was being told was MY mortgage lender. I asked if i could get their address and phone number to contact, and also to provide XXXX. To which she responded, " I dont know that info ''. When I inquired about the validity of a foreclosure sale-she told me she could not comment on that and would have to wait for her " servicer 's report. I told her I didnt understand what that meant and that I was working with a HUD counselor who had advised me there was a 5 week timeline requirement-which clearly we were outside of, as the conversation was being had on XX/XX/XXXX, with an alleged sales date of XX/XX/XXXX which I had no paperwork on and both her office and the local county sheriffs office had no record of any such paperwork being served by either offices-nor a request to deliver in the future. She told me she didnt know anything about a sheriffs sale but they would have their sale, but she could not comment on when that may or may not take place. I expressed my deep uneasiness with the lack of information from anyone yet a vague non committal reference to a potential sale by all parties I had reached out to. She said she didnt know what I was needing, and hung up on me. 
I reached back out to the HUD counselor who instructed me to attempt to log in my online account from my previous and last known mortgage company, XXXX XXXX to see if I had received any correspondence to inform me of the sale of my mortgage and provide me with the information that AmeriHome was now my new lender and their contact info, also when this might have taking place. I attempted to access my previous account but was denied access. Due to the continued lack of information and general confusion, and nearly purposeful uncooperative nature or willingness for any of the involved parties to take responsibility and give direction as to the the actual mortgage servicer, status of loan, or foreclosure, and scheduled sale/and or remediation options, the HUD counselor informed me she would like to bring my situation to one of her supervisors. At the end of the business day she called back with some advice from her supervisor and her opinion that my previous lender, XXXXXXXX XXXX and/or my new lender, which was determined to be AmeriHome-had neglected to properly and accurately transfer my loan for servicing. Among the issues Ive stated, and in addition to-My forbearance period and dates were not correctly accounted for, and the extension was not included nor mentioned to the new servicer. This seemingly has caused the appearance of longer delinquent period, over 90 days, than the mortgage in actuality was at the time AmeriHome bought it, in-what we now learned from the Notice of Sale document we called BACK to the law office for the 5th time and were able to request, after being specifically advised what to ask for by the HUD supervisor-on exactly XX/XX/2022. The day the XXXX program launch for applications to be submitted and I subsequently submitted my application, at that time showing XXXXXXXX XXXX as my mortgage lender, which they were. 
I am now working with the HUD counselor to proceed with options to equip myself with the pending sale. I am beyond flabbergasted and appalled at the treatment I have received thus far and the seemingly nearly purposeful concealment of information I have the right to as a consumer, particularly concerning my largest purchase to date in my XXXX years, and undoubtedly my greatest asset. Aside from the blatantly inconsiderate and counterproductive unprofessional encounters I have had thus far-can we for a moment consider the cruelty to be so flippant and irresponsible regarding another persons home?! I am a XXXX  mom with XXXX children, who saved my entire down payment myself while making {$12.00}, prior to being laid off during XXXX I had never been late or missed a single payment on my mortgage. The day I closed on my home is and was one of the best moments of my entire life. I take great pride in the fact I was able to give my children a safe, consistent, and stable place where we dont have to rely on anyone or be separated due to lack of space or affordable housing in the rental market. I am astounded that the customer service, providing of information I can not otherwise obtain, and the literal battle to be given what should if nothing else, and surely not short of LEGALLY is due me. Ive had far better service at almost any drive thru Ive been too at this point then I am receiving from the holder of my mortgage. I have been physically Ill with worry and anxiety over the situation alone, and meet with an almost sabotaging agenda principle to merely gain information, I am apparently being held responsible for holding-yet it is literally being withheld creates a rather desperate and counterproductive futile chasing of ones own tail-so to speak. Considering that Foreclosures, are by their very nature a time sensitive and time obligated occurrences, it is simply unacceptable to allow lenders, services, and the third parties they employ to fulfill tasks on their behalf, to continue to operate with such a flagrant disregard and negligence for the consumers right to information, resolution options, timely and transparent access to documents, and contact information that can prevent the default or foreclosure of their mortgage loans. Particularly in regards to undermining the help for FHA and other government backed loans, when such allocated funds become available-especially following any national or world crisis, such as we saw and continue to see with XXXX XXXX. It is my sincere hope that the remainder of my attempt to work with the mortgage lender now holding me seemingly hostage in an active Foreclosure, will prove a better experience than the lack of such diligences and void of business principles and their seemingly unimportant integrity to adhere has brought us to this day. 

Thank you greatly for your time and consideration in this matter. My apologies for the overly wordy and unedited copy-I was not planning to share in the depth at which this became. I truly am shocked and concerned for my fellow American homeowners, who have gone or will go through a similar experience with their lender or this particular servicer. I doubt most have the tenacity to even continue to pursue what should not be a scavenger hunt of wasted precious time and energy to obtain in the first place. I know I have been left with an overwhelming sense of mistrust, disregard, and almost malicious opposition where I never imagined I would. Shame on me.

The representatives on the phone assured me the card was cancelled, and told me I would be receiving another card shortly. He told me that there had been ATM withdraws in XXXX XXXX, Nevada. I told them I had not been to XXXX XXXX in at least one and a half years and there was no way I made those withdrawals. They asked me what the last transaction I made was. I told them it was a debit at a thrift store in XXXX XXXX, California on XX/XX/XXXX. They asked me to look at each transaction and tell them if I recognized them. Only then did I realize the extent of the unauthorized transactions. I looked back and discovered several ATM withdrawals per day for {$80.00} each, all of them made in XXXX XXXX Nevada, with most of them being initiated before I lost my card. I was very clear with everyone I spoke to that these unauthorized transactions could not have any relation whatsoever to the card being lost on XX/XX/XXXX. They were separate issues. They asked and I told them that I never gave anyone my pin. I never let anyone use my card. I did not authorize these transactions. The representative on the phone told me there were cameras at the ATMs so they would be able to view those to determine whether this was me. I expressed great concern that these unauthorized transactions were not caught earlier by the bank since I was making transactions in my hometown, hundreds of miles away on the same days and at similar times using the same card, and there 's only one card. I asked that they note this for the investigator and they said they did. I was told I would receive a document that outlined the unauthorized transactions, and that I should review that and if it was correct, send it back signed and they would analyze my claim after that. I never received any document to sign and return. I received a text from my bank on XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX PM asking if I made an {$80.00} withdrawal on XX/XX/XXXX. Of course I had not made any withdrawal since earlier that day when I had called and cancelled the card. I did not notice the text until XX/XX/XXXX. I responded " NO ''. A representative from Chase called me immediately after that text. I answered and they asked me about several more ATM withdrawals that had occurred AFTER I had called on XX/XX/XXXX to cancel my card. I asked why someone was being allowed to withdraw money from my account if I had cancelled the card. The representative seemed confused and told me I had NOT cancelled the card. I had just made a claim about unauthorized transactions. Then she noticed that a new card was already being sent to me, and she apologized and said that for whatever reason the card did not actually get cancelled. She assured me it was now cancelled and nobody would be able to use it again. I had to hang up at that point because I was needed in court ( I 'm an XXXX XXXX and a Judge was motioning for me to come back in the court room ). On XX/XX/XXXX I received a text from my bank telling me that they had decided to give me a temporary credit on my account of {$0.00}. I called customer service to inquire why. I was placed on hold for over 5 minutes, and when the representative came back on the line, she told me that the {$0.00} credit was a mistake and that the credit would post to my account within a few days. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received an email from my bank telling me that they had investigated and determined that these transactions were " valid '' and that my claim had been denied. I called customer service on XX/XX/XXXX to inquire as to the details of why their investigation led them to this determination. Two different representatives told me there were three specific reasons that led to this determination : ( 1 ) I reported that the card was " lost '' ( as opposed to stolen ) on a date prior to the date of the last authorized transaction ; ( 2 ) I told them that I did not give the pin to anyone and I did not write it down anywhere ; and ( 3 ) I could not provide a reason as to how someone else would have my pin. In other words, they determined that it must 've been me making these withdrawals since I did n't lose the card until XX/XX/XXXX. They would not tell me what their definition of " valid '' was. When I asked if they had considered any other facts, such as the fact that these ATM withdrawals happened at the same time that I was making transactions in my hometown, they would not answer me or they answered " no ''. When I asked if they had reviewed the videos from the ATMs where the withdrawals were made, they would not answer me or they answered " no '' and told me I had to subpoena those videos. I asked them to send me the tapes of the conversations I had with the claims department and they refused. I asked them to send me documentation of the details of the investigation and they said I would receive them in about 10 business days. In total, there were XXXX unauthorized ATM withdrawals made on my account between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. Each of them was for {$80.00}. That 's a total of {$1600.00} that was taken from me while my bank stood by and watched. The unauthorized withdrawals have ceased now.

state: I had a checking account with Wells Fargo back in XXXX up until I believe it was XXXX. I deposited a check that was given to me from a person I know. That check was given to him from his lawyers estate account. It was for {$5000.00}. I already had a account with my money in it too. I deposited the check through the atm at night. I didn't take any money out at all. I also deposited {$100.00} cash throught the atm. Like I said I never took a dime out that night. The next day I went to get food for my kids and swiped the card it said declined. I called the bank and they told me my account had been shut down for fraud. I said what fraud. They told me for the {$5000.00} check that had been deposited the night before. The check was not in my name but my friends name. He had signed the check for me to deposit it. The money was to go to someone else and I was the only person that could get it to him. I told the bank that I needed that check back. They told me that it was being held and it was being investigated. I told them well I want my money that I also already had in the account and the cash I had deposited that night. They told me that I had to talk to the fraud department. I called the fraud department and got the run around there too. I told him I needed my money back from my account and the check. They said the only way I could get the check back is if the person whos check it was written out to came in with a license to get it. That person had left town and was going to be gone a while and I was to handle things for that person and thats why I was given the check. They said that they couldnt give it to me. I talked to the lawyer who gave that person the check because it was from the lawyers account. They wouldn't give it back to the lawyer either even thought it was his check. The lawyer even told them that I was supposed to have the check and confirmed everything. I asked the guy on the phone with the fraud department that I needed all the rest of money that was in my bank account prior to that check and also the cash I had deposited that night. They kept telling me that they had to wait for the investigation to finish and they were holding all my money. Im a XXXX mother with XXXX boys and they took all my money shut my account and wouldn't give me nothing of mine claiming I did fraud when I didn't. I called the manager at the Well Fargo and told her I wanted the money that was already in there and they put me and my kids without any money. She told me that she would send me the final statement with a check for my funds. I got the letter about a week later with just a closing statement and no check. I kept calling and would get the run around. I spoke to the manager again. She lied and said she never said she was sending me a check and kept telling me there is nothing she can do I have to call the fraud dept. I called them again and once again they refused to give me my money. I got so fed up and stressed out about it I finally had to just let it go and let them steal my money. This all happened in XXXX or XXXX. Then out of no where I get a letter from Wells Fargo in XXXX stating that they messed up and shut my account down for fraud when it wasn't and they made a mistake. They gave me a {$150.00} they said for my funds that were in there and a some to make up for their mess up. Seriously!!! I had more than that in my account and they want to give me less and what like {$50.00} for their mess up. Actually they gave me nothing for their mess up and didn't even give me back all the money I had in my account before they wrongfully closed my account without notice or anything. If I owed them money best believe I would have to pay interest on all that money for as long as it took for me to pay them back. They already put me through a lot of stress and problems by leaving me and my kids without any money and closing my account for no reason. Then they basically slap me in the face with this letter admitting they messed up 7 years later and on top of it not even give me all my money back and say they gave some to make up for their total XXXX up that really left me and my kids in a bad spot!! I would like to sue them. They stole my money and apologized later and gave me back just a little of it. I never deposited the check in hopes of sueing them. I figured if I deposited the check it might be agreeing with the amount they gave me and I might not be able to make them be held accountable for this crime. I still have the letter and the check they sent me. I would like to know what I can do to get all my money plus interest for the XXXX they put me and my kids through for no reason. Its crazy that a bank can just steal anyones money like that and they get away with it. I want something done about it. Im sure it has happened to a lot more people than me and someone needs to speak up about these companies getting away with stealing peoples hard earn money and leaving them without any.

My original complaint was met with a response from the company that was patently absurd, completely different from what I was informed on the phone and I would like someone else to review the complaint. 

My previous complaint was abruptly " closed with explanation '' on this website as if the company and I had resolved the matter, when in fact the company was so egregious in its own response they chose to NOT have their response open to the public, instead hidden from view. 

I challenged the company 's response and heard nothing back whatsoever ; as if they could just forget about the complaint since the CFPB waits for thousands of similar complaints against the same company to act upon trends. 

Previous complaint in its entirety : Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, On XX/XX/2018 I received a report from my XXXX   credit management account that my credit details had changed ; XXXX  noted that my 18 year old credit card account with XXXX ( Account # XXXX ) had suddenly closed without warning. This was a credit card account I had been actively using every month, used less than 1 % of the extended credit ( {$13000.00} ), and faithfully paid off the balance every month. The XX/XX/2018 paper billing statement ( attached to this as a PDF ) from the credit card company XXXX mailed to me ( statement date XX/XX/2018 due on XX/XX/2018 ) said nothing of closing the account or needing to extend the account date. I called the number on the XXXX  credit card ( XXXX ) for further information. After verifying my account, I was told my credit account was closed due to returned mail concerning renewing the account. I never received an e-mail or a phone call to verify the return to sender mail and I was still receiving their same monthly paper billing statement in the mail as I did every month ( it wasnt being returned to them and it had the exact same mailing address they had on file ). The expiration date on the card was XX/XX/2018 and I asked if we could simply reinstate the account, but I was told emphatically that it was impossible to do so and the ONLY way to continue doing business with XXXX was to open and reestablish a new credit card account. I escalated my concerns and spoke to a manager, but he replied with the same excuse ; the account was closed ONLY because they received back the letter ( return to  sender ) they had sent to extend the account. The manager then said he could send a letter stating the same. My reply was how would he know if that letter would even make it to me in the mail or get returned? He agreed and I explained to him how ludicrous the situation was, what my credit concerns were and the fact that I would report this to the ConsumerFinancial Protection Bureau. I even asked how could an 18 year old credit account be closed due to something as petty as returned mail without some kind of human oversight ; ( I am a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Virginia XXXX ) meaning no business I know or operated would think about closing an active, 18 year old account with NO derogatory actions without reviewing it first especially if there were no way to reverse the action. My concerns with the above are twofold : 1. I  have just lost an 18 year old credit account on my credit file. I am XXXX years old and had three long term open credit accounts ( 15+ years each ), maintain a low to mid 800 FICO with all three credit reporting companies, paid off my prior mortgages, no car payment, have no other debts and pay every credit account in full every month. Now I only have two active accounts in my credit file. Lose - Lose Situation With My Credit a. Closing the account will adversely affect my credit ratings, lower my FICO scores which will cost me money and individual negotiating power via higher APR rates and less attractive loan level pricing adjustments/credit offers in the future ( according to all three credit reporting companies ). b. I would certainly understand closing the account if I violated the terms we had agreed to ; late payment/no payment, inactive account, over extend credit, etc. But, in this case I did nothing wrong. It seems as if they wanted to open a new account with a dubious industry close and switch tactic so they can change the rate and terms to favor them better in the 10 pages of new fine print. Obviously, thats difficult to prove from where I sit, but it seems as the only likely motive for closing such a long standing account without human oversight. I understand other citizens have more important situations and there is nothing you can do to reinstate the account, but I feel I have a legitimate complaint about this financial giants industry tactics and would like them noted in the public record somewhere and have this information sent from your bureau over to a complaint review board/executive process at XXXX  for their review ; if it ever would make it that far or ever get the attention it deserves. Thank you for your help with this matter. Cordially, XXXX XXXX.

I 'm currently preparing to apply for graduate school. I pay my XXXX loans monthly to XXXX and XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I was notified of a hold on my XXXX XXXX University account preventing the release of transcripts when I attempted to have them sent to another school. 

I called the following day ( XX/XX/XXXX ) to inquire, and was told by my University that my XXXX loan  was 24 months past due and had been sent to collections. 

I was surprised. I had never received a bill for this loan or any contact about it. The university representative explained that my mailing address had been changed twice, which I had not done. She said it had been changed internally. The original mailing address was correct, so I have no idea where anything has been sent for two years. They also had an outdated phone number that has n't been in use since XX/XX/XXXX. 

However, she said, because I had opted for electronic notification, statements were being sent to my university email account. 

Having been out of school for three years, I retrieved my university email account. I found zero  emails had been sent to me in regards to this loan. 

I did receive many emails asking me to sign the exit interview, the most recent from XX/XX/XXXX. I remember these emails because despite having signed it multiple times, it was never processed through XXXX 's poor website. It eventually worked, however XXXX still shows that I 've never signed it. 

So, I used the Live Chat feature on XXXX 's website after reading horrendous reviews about their phone-based customer service. This Live Chat did not answer my questions and, at the end, was edited by XXXX and does not reflect the actual transcript. Below is the transcript, and please note the edits XXXX made to this conversation : Chat transcription : XXXX XXXX XXXX : Hello XXXX, thank you for using Live Chat! One moment please while I access your account. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : Hi there! Thanks. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : I have now accessed your account, how may I assist you today? 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : I actually just found out about this account today. Apparently, I 'm two years past due, but have never received a letter, email, or bill in relation to this loan. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : This account has been assigned to collections and XXXX XXXX  is no longer servicing it. The loan is now with XXXX XXXX XXXX. and you can contact them at XXXX for assistance. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : Can you tell me why I never received a bill? 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : Did you have a valid mailing address on the account during the time it was with XXXX  XXXX? 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : I don't know, since I never knew about this account. If all information came from my University, then there should have been. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : Either way, you will need to contact XXXX XXXX XXXX., we can not assist you with this account. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : I understand and appreciate the phone number. However, I still do not understand why Heartland never contacted me about this loan. If it 's not in collections, which affects my finances, this is a major concern. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : Now in collections* XXXX XXXX XXXX : The account show bills as having been mail every month to ( correct mailing address was here ) throughout XX/XX/XXXX. 

XXXXMy replies, which were not read nor responded to by XXXX : XXXX XXXX : That is the correct address, thank you for checking. However, I never received anything. 
XXXX Sir, Im going to assume youre a real person and not a robot. Ive known about this loan for about two hours, and in that time Ive found a wealth of information online about others who - like me - never received bills in relation to their loans. I dont want the headache of contacting the XXXX or Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, or calling a lawyer. I want information about what methods were used to contact me, and records of them. 

XXXXThe next update to the chat erased my previous two messages. XXXX 's responses appeared in the chat transcript with inconsistent time stamps, not in the chat itself. These replies did not appear until the chat had ended : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX : Also, late letters and phone calls were issued throughout the year. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : The account was reassigned to collections in early XX/XX/XXXX. 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : May I assist you with anything else today, XXXX? 
XXXX XXXX XXXX : I do apologize, due to no further response I will be ending the chat. If you are still in need of assistance, please do not hesitate to begin a new Live Chat session with us or you can also contact our office by calling XXXX and any of our representatives will be more than happy to assist you. We are here Monday-Friday from XXXX XXXX-XXXX XXXX Eastern Standard Time in our Call Center and we are available on Live Chat Monday-Friday from XXXX XXXX-XXXX XXXX and also on Saturday from XXXX XXXX-XXXX XXXX. Again, we do apologize we missed you but look forward to assisting you in the future. Have a great day and thank you for using Live Chat! 


My concerns are three : 1. XXXX XXXX has a near-unanimous reputation from consumers for being deceitful, difficult, disrespectful, and cutting corners. I do not understand how they 're still contracted to handle student loans by public, government-funded institutions.

2. My mailing address given to XXXX has been my parent 's home for eleven years. That it was internally changed twice to non-existent addresses seems incredibly odd, especially since I received my diploma in the mail without issue. Further, that XXXX in the Live Chat claimed my original address was what they had on file makes no sense. XXXX 's office informed me that XXXX had a different address. Before I could log in to the Live Chat, I had to provide my address. I believe the address XXXX provided during the chat was copied from this form, and they lied.

The original balance was small, only {$1000.00}, but now totals over {$1500.00} due to late fees for bills I never received. I received zero  emails, phone calls, letters, bills, or any form of contact. The last email about my loan was as stated earlier, on XX/XX/XXXX, asking me to once again sign the exit interview from XXXX. I have not received any contact from XXXX XXXX XXXX or XXXX about this loan. 

I have a major ethical issue with so many universities across the country using this universally detested and shady company for collecting on debts. Yes, collections agencies get a bad reputation. But what XXXX  XXXX has done to many consumers, including myself, is wrong. They are clearly comfortable making continuous clerical errors in order to turn profits off of fees. I was shocked to see the Live Chat transcript edited so heavily, but after reading dozens and dozens of stories about this company I 'm no longer surprised and simply disappointed in my university for using this company in the first place.

When I applied for the PSLF, I obtained the required Employer Verification and started paying through this program. I have taught at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, a XXXX, XXXX XXXX recognized employer, for over 25 years. I have far exceeded the XXXX qualifying payments in my public service, making on-time payments over decades. 

As for this particular program and its eligibility, I have been told on more than one occasion, that I qualified for the PSLF program and my Employment Verification was up to date. A few years ago I called again to make sure that payments were qualifying and was told no, that I was enrolled in the wrong payment program and that none of my payments count towards the PSLF. To date, I have accrued only XXXX qualifying payments. And today I discovered that because I failed to re-certify my XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, my current payment will not count either. I have been making qualifying payments for the last few years ( let alone the last 20+ ), how could they not count towards the PSLF? I wonder if there is a class action suit against this entity yet for people who are doing all they can to qualify, certify, etc. for a plan that, at every turn in the road, seems to be nearly impossible to achieve? CREDIT CORP SOLUTIONS XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I checked my XXXX credit reports and found an assumed collection account XXXX @ {$260.00} with CREDIT CORP SOLUTIONS with different opening dates, balances, first date of delinquency, balance due, and/or last date of activities for this same exact account number. I have never had an account with this company nor any record of any type of first notice of debt including rights to dispute from this company. And if I, by chance, even though I have no recollection nor tangible record, naively spoke with a representative of this company over the phone about this debt, I was not informed by that representative that I had a right to dispute this debt nor a specific timeframe to do so.

15 USC 1692g 809. Validation of debts ( a ) Notice of debt ; contents states that within XXXX days after the initial communication with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt, a debt collector shall, unless the following information is contained in the initial communication or the consumer has paid the debt, send the consumer a written notice containing ( XXXX ) a statement that unless the consumer, within XXXX days after receipt of the notice, disputes the validity of the debt, or any portion thereof, the debt will be assumed to be valid by the debt collector. XXXX XXXX XXXX definition of the word receipt is- a writing acknowledging the receiving of goods or money ; proof, evidence. I never signed nor received any type of acknowledgement receipt from a mailing service for any mail from this company. I am familiar with the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ). Had I signed a receipt of notice for the proper and legal documentation from this company, I wouldve immediately responded asking for lawful verification of debt or copy of court ordered judgement well within the lawful XXXX days allotted. After receiving my response letter with receipt, t

his company would have to legally cease from collection attempts and remove the account from my credit reports until their proof of verification is sent back to me. This company has reported to my credit reports without observing the FDCPA laws. My credit has been impacted adversely because of this companys irresponsibility. My credit reports also show that CREDIT CORP SOLUTIONS has provided this alleged account with inaccurate information. The FCRA requires that all data reported from the credit reporting agencies, creditors, or furnishers on a consumer 's report be 100 % ACCURATE, 100 % VERIFIABLE, and 100 % TIMELY. This means no data can be reported that can't be legally PROVEN to be 100 % accurate. I also understand that medical collections under {$500.00}, a paid medical collection, a collection less than a year old, or having a past due balance found on a collection account should not be listed on consumer credit
reports. My XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX credit reports all show different and inaccurate open dates, balances, first date of delinquency, balance due, and/or last date of activities for this same exact account.

This is erroneous and flawed reporting that is listed on my credit reports. Not only did CREDIT CORP SOLUTIONS not follow lawful FDCPA communications protocol, but it has also broken FDCPA False or Misleading Representations protocol as well. A debt collector, in collecting a debt, may not use any false, deceptive, or misleading representation. Specifically, a debt collector may not falsely represent the character, amount, or legal status of the debt, or of any services rendered, or compensation he or she may receive for collecting the debt. A debt collector may not communicate, or threaten to communicate, false credit information or information that should be known to be false, including not identifying disputed debts as such. Each of my XXXX credit reports show different information instead of them all showing the exact same information. This is considered a false and misleading representation that this company has submitted to the credit reporting agencies.

Please remove this account from my credit reports immediately. It is not my duty to provide evidence that this alleged debt is not mine. It is the obligation of the debt collector to provide evidence that they can lawfully collect on any alleged debt, accurately report to the credit agencies, and follow all FCRA and FDCPA laws. As of today, they have been unsuccessful.
